# DSH Studio 0.9.8-plus4

The same-site shell, hardened: the loopback cookie pile stays bounded, and the
frame cannot silently fall back out of the site it needs to share.

This build carries exactly the shell/cookie/announcement code proposed
upstream in [Moresyl/dsh-studio#15](https://github.com/Moresyl/dsh-studio/pull/15)
(five commits), so what you run here is what upstream is being asked to merge.

## Fixed and added

- **Loopback cookies are swept before every Harness process, not once at app
  start.** dsh plants a fresh, randomly-named auth cookie at every boot and
  retires none of the ones before it; each is good for thirty days, cookies
  ignore ports, and the whole pile rides on every request the window makes.
  The Harness serves from a plain `node:http` server whose default
  request-header ceiling is 16 KiB — roughly seventy of these cookies — so a
  window left open for days reaches it after enough restarts. The sweep now
  runs at the one safe moment: after the previous session is gone and before
  the next is minted, covering launches, crash restarts and version switches.
- **An announced Harness address that spells the host out is rewritten.**
  `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are different sites to a cookie (SameSite
  compares scheme and registrable domain, and a name is not an address), so
  taking the announcement as printed would put the embedded frame back into
  the third-party context this design exists to leave — with the original 401
  as its only symptom. The launch always binds `127.0.0.1`; the bootstrap
  token is preserved.

## Verification

- 388 Rust tests and 269 frontend tests pass; clippy `-D warnings` clean.
  The server's round-trip tests include a 137 KB cookie header.
- Built as a universal macOS bundle and launched against Harness 0.1.5-rc.2:
  the window loads from the loopback server and the workspace comes up
  authenticated.
- A cookieless request to the Harness still answers 401 — the fence is intact.

## Install

Download the package for your platform below. macOS builds are universal and
ad-hoc signed: on first launch, right-click the app and choose "Open". On
Windows, choose "Run anyway" if SmartScreen warns.
